title: The refrigerator engineer, the armless archer, and the ship built for six kilometres down. September 22, 2026.
excerpt: From a widowed actress who broke a taboo in 1931 to a climate scientist who started in a factory, September 22's five stories share one thread: none of these people entered their field through the front door.
bodyHtml:
None of today's five subjects had an easy way in. Each one found a side door, and then made the room bigger once they were through it.

September 22, 1991: the widow who broke a taboo just to survive

Durga Khote died in Mumbai on September 22, 1991, at age 86. Born into a respectable, English-educated family in 1905, she was widowed at 26 with two young sons to raise. In 1931 she took a minor role in the silent film Farebi Jaal - a profession her own class considered disreputable for a woman of her background. She went on to act in roughly 200 films across five decades, most famously as Jodhabai in Mughal-e-Azam, and in 1983 received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award, Indian cinema's highest honor.

An executive with zero gaming experience now runs Xbox

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced on February 20, 2026 that Asha Sharma would become CEO of Microsoft Gaming, succeeding Phil Spencer - leading Xbox, Bethesda and Activision Blizzard, a division reaching roughly 500 million monthly active users. Sharma had never worked in video games before; her background in AI and user growth, built across Cargill, Deloitte, Microsoft, Meta and Instacart, was the stated reason for her selection as Xbox faced a 7% revenue decline and a missed Game Pass growth target.

Born without arms, she became the best archer alive

Sheetal Devi, from a small village in Jammu and Kashmir, was born with phocomelia and had never seen a bow before age 15. A physical test revealed unusual upper-body strength; she took up archery in 2021, learning to draw and release with her feet and shoulder. At the Paris 2024 Paralympics, aged 17, she became India's youngest-ever Paralympic medallist, and in March 2026 she won the compound women's world title at the World Archery Para Championships - the first armless woman in history crowned a world para archery champion.

The refrigerator engineer who rewrote climate science

Veerabhadran Ramanathan, born in Madurai in 1944, worked as an engineer at a refrigerator factory in Secunderabad before turning to atmospheric science. He was the first to show that CFCs - known only for depleting the ozone layer - were also powerful greenhouse gases, and identified the vast 'brown clouds' of soot over South Asia that disrupt monsoon rainfall. In 2026, the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded him the Crafoord Prize in Geosciences, sometimes called the 'Nobel of Geosciences,' worth roughly $900,000.

A ship built to go where no one's fully charted yet

India launched its first fully indigenous ocean research vessel, ORV Sagar Manthan, on September 9, 2026, at GRSE's Rishi Bankim Shipyard in Kolkata. Built under the Deep Ocean Mission at a cost of roughly ₹840 crore, the 89.5-metre, 5,900-tonne vessel is rated to survey up to six kilometres deep in the roughest seas on Earth, including the Southern Ocean - its job is mapping the Indian Ocean's mid-ocean ridges and evaluating deep-sea mineral resources.

Five stories, one thread: a taboo broken out of necessity, a turnaround entrusted to an outsider, a body written off as a limitation, a factory floor that led to a Nobel-adjacent prize, and a vessel headed somewhere nobody's mapped. None of today's five people were given the obvious path. Each one built a different way in, and it held.
